title: In 20 larval zebrafish, mapZebrain wiring predicts region coupling beyond distance and region effects; near swim bouts all spatial structure of coupling increases
abstract: Question: in the larval zebrafish brain, does the region wiring diagram predict functional coupling (FC) between regions after distance and region effects are removed, and does this wiring slope change with swimming or with dark flashes? Earlier campaign work in mouse found a 24% smaller wiring slope during task engagement. Data: processed whole-brain two-photon calcium imaging of 22 larvae with tail video (Legare et al. 2025, CC BY 4.0) and the released mapZebrain SC (65 regions, 2,080 pairs). Method: FC = Fisher-z correlation of region dF/F; model FC = node fixed effects + distance terms + beta x SC; swim and flash contrasts used equal numbers of 6-volume blocks per fish; fish were the unit of inference. Results: on fish-mean quiet FC the SC partial r was 0.16 (shuffle null 0.00 +/- 0.02, p = 0.0005), positive in 17 of 20 fish, and 0.13-0.14 in two other released FC sets (one from Chen et al. 2018 light-sheet data). SC added only 0.8% of FC variance beyond node effects and distance. In 12 fish, the wiring slope near swim bouts was 1.56 times the quiet slope (CI 1.08-2.55; partial r 0.119 vs 0.080, p = 0.027), also after removal of the swim-triggered response, for three window lengths and in every leave-one-fish-out fit. This is the opposite direction to the mouse result. But the increase was not specific to wiring: coupling with closeness rose from 0.26 to 0.35 (11 of 12 fish) and coupling with gene co-expression also rose without global signal regression. Dark flashes did not change the slope (ratio 1.06, CI 0.67-1.68); a spontaneous-block control varied by about 30%. Limitations: 12 fish for the swim contrast, small effects, possible motion artefacts during swims, coarse undirected SC from sparse tracings, 1 Hz imaging; some checks were added after the main swim result.

display.caption: Wiring and quiet FC. A: raw SC-FC relation of fish-mean quiet FC (colour = distance). B: residuals after node fixed effects and distance (orange: decile means). C: partial r of SC with FC with distance controls only and with node effects + distance, in three FC data sets, with the 95% range of a distance-decile SC shuffle.

Condition contrasts with block matching. A, B: per-fish partial r and slope beta in each condition (orange) and its reference (green). C: ratio of mean wiring slopes with fish-bootstrap 95% CIs, for the primary contrasts and swim robustness checks; the dashed line is the mouse VBN engaged/passive ratio from campaign study 63daa564.

A: SC partial r for ongoing quiet FC and for event-locked FC (dark-flash cycle averages, swim-triggered averages). B: per-fish block-matched swim versus quiet coupling with wiring, wiring after gene co-expression, gene co-expression, and closeness (-log distance, node effects only). Bars are means.

citations.reason: All imaging data, swim detector output, SC matrices, atlas files, gene expression and two group FC matrices (CC BY 4.0).
Source paper of the data and SC matrices; we extend its SC-FC result with node fixed effects, distance controls and state contrasts.
We followed its dF/F, region exclusion and swim alignment procedures.
mapZebrain atlas and single-neuron tracings behind the SC matrices.
Light-sheet data behind the source authors' FC_matrix_lightsheet, used for replication.

Earlier campaign zebrafish projectome-FC test. We support its positive specifications (pair-specific link 0.13-0.16 in three FC sets, including Chen 2018 data) and challenge its primary whole-recording null and its null for stimulus-locked FC (we find 0.12 for dark-flash cycles).
Mouse VBN: engagement decreased the wiring slope by 24%. In zebrafish, swim-related states increased it (ratio 1.56), so the direction does not generalise across these animals and states.
Mouse IBL: decision task did not change the wiring slope; comparison of state effects.
Mouse fMRI: tracer-FC coupling depends on anaesthesia state; comparison of state effects.
Cross-species connectome-FC work with node fixed effects and distance controls (worm, fly, mouse, marmoset, human); this adds zebrafish.
